primary_reading_extent.extent_and_limits: Read the one-page professional author bibliography, including the 1982, 1991 and 1994 entries. It supplies dates and credits only. Later translated and revised manifestations remain distinct.

Read three first-person opening paragraphs displayed as “Extract, ” corresponding to the opening on 89. This is authored primary essay text. It supports only the explicit use of the conquest of Mexico and its texts to investigate attitudes toward other societies. The full article and The Conquest of America remain unread; 2024 is the online posting date.
Read the authority fields: birth on 1 March 1939 in Sofia and death on 7 February 2017 in Paris. The record distinguishes Cvetan Todorov (1899–1962).

Read the complete short attributed essay, especially “An act of faith in the future.” Its 12 October 2018 posting is posthumous and creates no new authorship or contribution date. Historical examples remain part of Todorov’s ethical argument rather than independent event verification.

Checked the indexed institutional title, translator and original-publication note: New York, Harper & Row, 1984. The current 1999 manifestation is distinct from the 1982 French original and first English publication in 1984. The body remains unread.

relationship_scope.claim: Uses conquest as a historical case for examining attitudes toward other societies
relationship_scope.evidence: The three authored opening paragraphs of “The Morality of Conquest, ” printed 89, explicitly identify the conquest of Mexico and its texts as the case. This limited methodological connection does not assert the unread book’s full thesis or label Todorov a member of a later school.

relationship_scope.claim: Challenges the assumption that remembering victimhood necessarily prevents violence
relationship_scope.evidence: Own UNESCO essay distinguishes selective remembrance from ethical use and warns that former victims can become aggressors. This is his bounded intervention on public memory, not a psychological finding or a universal judgment on victims.
